text: Software is cheaper to generate. But a feature is more than a prompt. It must match the behavior you need, fit your product, and survive tests.
AYA starts with your repository and a reference. Here, the request is concrete: bring Fireworks SQL tools into a working Crusoe cookbook.

Native Hermes investigates pinned reference behavior through REA in OpenShell, then implements the contract. This SQL example uses source and runtime analysis. Each action becomes inspectable evidence.
The first component passed one hundred seventeen checks. One failure blocked delivery. A repair passed all one hundred eighteen, including a fresh evaluation.
The result is a real GitHub pull request with passing continuous integration and fifty four target tests. The delivered component powers actual Crusoe queries over live repository data.

Now improve the factory itself. MASS proposed a new workflow. On public SQL development tasks, the bare model scored twelve of twelve. Both native workflows scored eleven. The retained workflow passed three of six held out.
The evidence selected all twelve verified baseline answers. One call instead of twenty two on development. Ten training answers and two validation answers produced a real Crusoe student checkpoint.

MASS alternates workflow search with training, then repeats with updated weights. We demonstrated search, verified answer selection, and training. Serving and evaluation are next. No recursive improvement is claimed.
